correctness.rationale: For nonzero mutually orthogonal projections the rotated real part is exactly a direct sum of scalar eigenvalues a*cos(theta) and b*cos(theta-beta). The squared norm is the maximum of their squares, including an optional zero block. The identity max(u,v)=(u+v+|u-v|)/2 and the exact mean absolute-sinusoid integral give equation (1). Strict differentiation in s=sin(beta) establishes uniqueness of extrema. The normalized arctan integral has a strictly decreasing ratio to s³; its endpoint values give both globally best constants. Taylor expansion and uniform epsilon-scaling establish the cubic law and crossover without relying on numerical checks. A current-attachment standard-library checker passed 909 finite assertions, including quadrature, phase bounds, sharp coefficient samples and crossover. Finiteness is never used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The first genuinely two-eigenvalue unequal-modulus normal class of a newly studied angular numerical radius has two natural invariant parameters: radial contrast and projective spectral angle. An exact full profile identifies sharp angular extremizers and two globally optimal cubic stability constants; the singular double-scaling law explains the transition to the covered equal-modulus linear regime. This is a motivated complete quantitative family, not an arbitrary sample or an isolated small improvement. No all-normal-spectrum or all-operator generalization is claimed.
